title: micro-eval gating scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal notebook for an idea: introduce a lightweight, in-production micro-evaluation harness to gate model rollouts and fallbacks. Goal is to detect small but important regressions (hallucination rate, safety triggers, instruction-following) on a per-release basis without full-batch offline evals.

Motivation / problem:
- We push model variants frequently; current rollout relies mainly on perf metrics (p50/p95 latency, errors) and a small manual eval set.
- Subtle regressions in factuality and instruction compliance slip through until customers raise tickets.
- Running large eval suites for every commit is expensive and slow. Need fast signal that integrates into canaries.

High-level idea:
- Ship a micro-eval harness embedded in the Serving runtime that:
  - Samples a tiny, targeted set of checks per request stream (randomized, low rate).
  - Uses lightweight probes: short QA pairs, instruction-following prompts, and safety-pattern detectors.
  - Aggregates signals per model-version and per-route, computes rolling deltas vs baseline, and flags regressions to Rollout Controller.

User stories:
- As an SRE/ML engineer I want to see a daily micro-eval report per model so I can decide whether to pause a rollout.
- As a PM I want thresholds (relative drop in pass-rate) that trigger automated canary rollback so we avoid broad outages of correctness.
- As a privacy officer I want probes to never include customer data and remain synthetic/owned by Redwood.

Probe types (fast):
- Factual QA (1–2 sentence prompts with verifiable answers).
- Instruction compliance (e.g., "summarize in 2 bullets").
- Toxicity/safety heuristics (fast regex + small classifier).
- Structured extraction (schema conformance checks).

Architecture sketch:
- Probe generator: centrally managed corpus (small, tagged). Exposed via the control plane.
- Runtime hooks: sample X% of requests to attach a hidden probe in parallel (no latency impact on caller). Probe executes async and writes to micro-eval stream.
- Aggregator: lightweight service that computes pass-rate deltas, p-values, and simple drift metrics.
- Rollout integration: expose signals to Console + automatic gating policies (threshold-based or Bayesian).

Acceptance criteria / metrics:
- Warm-start signal within 30 minutes of a model switch for a mid-sized customer.
- Detects >20% drop in pass-rate on targeted probes with 95% confidence in 1h window.
- <0.1% additional cost in per-token serving spend for typical workloads.

Experiment ideas:
- Start internal-only: run on traffic from internal teams + synthetic traffic (no PII). Compare to offline evals to calibrate probe sensitivity.
- A/B canary: enable micro-eval on 10% of canary traffic and measure correlation with customer escalations.
- Feedback loop: surface false positives to a small annotation tool so we can refine probes.

Open questions / risks:
- Probe corpus maintenance: who owns tags and freshness? (prod-infra vs applied-ml)
- Statistical validity on low-traffic routes – need per-route minimum sample sizes or Bayesian priors.
- Safety/PII: ensure probe insertion never leaks to external logs or telemetry tied to customers.
- Ops complexity vs benefit: keep the first iteration narrow and opt-in.

Next steps (short):
1) Draft a tiny proto corpus (50 probes across 4 categories).
2) Spike a runtime hook that emits probe outcome to a temp topic.
3) Build a quick aggregator notebook that computes per-version pass-rate deltas.
4) Demo to applied-ml + SRE for feedback.

Notes to self:
- Keep everything synthetic and reversible.
- Consider integration with Redwood Optimize to suggest probes for workloads (e.g., high-embedding usage customers might need different checks).
- Ticket: create JIRA for prototype GH-PR-889 linking the aggregator.

References / quick links:
- CONFLUENCE-1234: "Eval framework design (v2)"
- JIRA-ENG-4521: "Canary rollback automation"
